topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing introduces the lecture series context and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications drive clonal fitness and Darwinian selection in early neoplastic tissue.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the cancer stem cell hypothesis and present experimental evidence for how tissue hierarchy and specific cells of origin influence tumor initiation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory influences on tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how chronic inflammation, paracrine signals, and supportive stromal interactions promote neoplastic progression and sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Technologies for investigating tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the laboratory, computational, and spatial profiling methods used to track mutational timing and cellular interactions within tumors.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational acquisition, cell-of-origin properties, and permissive microenvironmental conditions that drive malignant progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
